sweeps.notes:
Methodology: used WebSearch to find candidate pages, then WebFetch to pull exact figures/quotes from manufacturer spec sheets (Daikin Malaysia FTKF/FHC-A series), manufacturer support manuals (Samsung/Midea/Panasonic), retailer/price-comparison blogs, and energy-consultancy guides to TNB's RP4 tariff. 11 distinct domains covered: senheng.com.my, aircondlounge.com, seagullaire.com, acson.com.my, daikin.com.my (plus daikin-model mirrors on retailer sites), recommend.my, myaccool.com, samsung.com, calculatormalaysia.com, trexon.my, arusenerg.com, plusxnergy.com, paultan.org — well over the requested 6.

Key agreements vs disagreements:
- HP→BTU/kW conversion: all five independent conversion-table sources (senheng, aircondlounge, seagullaire, acson, Daikin's own catalogued models) agree on the same rough bands — 1.0HP≈9,000 BTU/h (~2.6-2.8kW), 1.5HP≈12,000-12,300 BTU/h (~3.4-3.8kW), 2.0HP≈18,000-19,000 BTU/h (~5.1-5.6kW), 2.5HP≈22,500-25,000 BTU/h (~6.0-7.3kW), 3.0HP≈24,000-30,000 BTU/h (~7.0-8.8kW). There is real spread because "HP" is a nameplate/motor-size label, not a regulated cooling-capacity unit — actual rated BTU for a given HP class varies by brand/model (e.g. Daikin's own 2.5HP model is rated 24,000 BTU while Daikin's 3.0HP model is only 25,600 BTU, barely above its own 2.5HP unit, showing HP labels are not strictly linear with capacity). Recommend treating "1HP=9,000 BTU/h, 1kW=3,412 BTU/h" as the universal rule-of-thumb, but sizing from actual spec-sheet BTU/kW, not the HP badge.
- COP/CSPF: Malaysia's MEPS/energy-label regime for units ≤7.1kW (i.e. up to ~2.5HP) uses CSPF (Wh/Wh), not simple COP; inverter units we found range CSPF 4.60 (1.0-1.5HP, 4-star) to 6.00 (2.5HP, 5-star). Non-inverter ducted/ceiling-exposed units (Daikin FHC-A series, which also covers sizes above 3HP equivalent, e.g. the 36,000–55,000 BTU/h models) report CSPF 3.11-3.45 and rated power input directly (1,785W-5,500W) — noticeably less efficient than inverter CSPF values, consistent with the general claim (myaccool.com) that a 5-star unit draws roughly half the power of a 3-star for the same load (1,400W vs 850W cited for a 1.5HP-equivalent load). No source gave a plain "COP" number for non-inverter units; CSPF/rated-power-input figures are what's actually published, so COP must be back-calculated as capacity(W)/power-input(W) from the spec sheet if needed.
- Lowest setpoint: three independent manufacturer manuals (Samsung, Midea, Panasonic) agree on 16°C as the standard minimum for ordinary split units, with Samsung's own page flagging that "the lowest setting temperature of the remote control may vary by country." One manufacturer note (Panasonic) describes a specialist "low-temp" ducted/cassette/under-ceiling product line engineered to run down to 8°C for applications needing deeper cooling (e.g. a mushroom room) — this is a distinct product, not a setting available on an ordinary split.
- Prices: no disagreement in kind, only breadth — non-inverter units run roughly RM600-2,000 across 1.0-2.0HP, inverter units roughly RM1,000-3,100 across the same range (calculatormalaysia.com, cross-checked against Daikin's own official RM3,940 (2.5HP) and RM4,560 (3.0HP) list prices). Ceiling cassette/ducted units above 3HP (4.0-6.0HP) run roughly RM6,000-9,800 installed-equipment price depending on inverter/non-inverter and series, per multiple Daikin-authorized retailer listings (DoubleK, Seng Huat, Seagull Aire, 1Now) — note these retailer prices were found via WebSearch synthesis rather than individually fetched per listing, so treat exact RM figures as indicative rather than verified line-by-line.
- TNB tariff: three independent sources (trexon.my, arusenerg.com, plusxnergy.com) agree closely on RP4 rates effective 1 July 2025: domestic (Tariff A) energy charge 27.03 sen/kWh (≤1,500kWh)/37.03 sen/kWh (>1,500kWh) + 4.55 sen/kWh capacity + 12.85 sen/kWh network ≈ 44.43/54.43 sen/kWh before AFA; commercial Low Voltage General ≈ 27.03 + 8.83 + 14.82 = 50.68 sen/kWh; Medium Voltage General 29.83 sen/kWh + RM89.27/kW demand charge; High Voltage General 43.03 sen/kWh + RM31.21/kW. On top of these base rates, a monthly AFA (Automatic Fuel Adjustment) surcharge/rebate applies — it was negative (a rebate, e.g. -4.99 sen/kWh in Jan 2026 per paultan.org) earlier in 2026 and turned into a small surcharge by mid-2026, reaching +3.61 sen/kWh in October 2026 per trexon.my — so the "current" effective domestic rate today (Oct 2026) is roughly 44.43 + 3.61 ≈ 48 sen/kWh for usage ≤1,500 kWh/month, before EEI rebates/service tax. No source disagreement found on the base RP4 rates themselves; the only real time-variation is the monthly AFA adjustment, which is expected and official (set by Energy Commission/ST), not a source conflict. I could not get a readable quote directly from TNB's own tariff booklet PDF (it fetched as corrupted binary) or mytnb.com.my (navigation-only page with no rate table rendered) — all tariff figures above come from independent secondary (but official-rate-citing) consultancy/energy-company sources, cross-checked against each other rather than against TNB's primary PDF.
Caveat: all "ac.price.*" and "ac.cassette/ducted price" entries reflect retail listing/search-snippet prices seen in Oct 2026 and are promotional/time-sensitive, not official RRPs except where explicitly noted as Daikin's own official site price.

sweeps.notes:
Coverage and method: I used WebSearch to locate candidates and WebFetch to read the actual pages wherever possible. Most grower-guide and academic figures above were independently fetched and quoted verbatim. A few entries are flagged explicitly as "unverified by direct fetch" where WebFetch returned HTTP 403/404/connection errors (academia.edu Thailand paper, Tridge export page, Mogoo Farm price, Dusun frozen price, the generic "core temperature / 35°C kill" grower-forum claim) — these came only from WebSearch's own synthesis of the page, not from a page I read myself, so treat them as lower-confidence and re-verify before using in a design spec.

Major disagreements found:
1. Spawn-run temperature: sources split between ~18-24°C (mushroomalmanac, out-grow standard, naturelion, mushroom-appreciation, fungiacademy, novamushrooms, growmushrooms.co) and 25-27°C (out-grow "warm-weather" strain; also the Thai Chiang Mai J. Sci./academia.edu paper's "25±2°C"); the one real lowland-tropical commercial farm I found data for (Fresh & Friendly Farm, Pathum Thani, Thailand — PMC10432537/Nature Sci Reports 2023) ran spawn run at a surprisingly cool 20°C with light, not dark, which disagrees with most hobbyist guides' "dark, 21-24°C" advice. Spawn-run duration varies hugely: 7 days (that same Thai commercial study) vs 10-21 days vs 2-5 weeks vs 30-40 days (academia.edu, unverified) — likely strain- and scale-dependent, and the 7-day figure may just mean "to visible full-bottle colonization" rather than a fully mature, pin-ready block.
2. Cold-shock trigger: standard strains need a deliberate temperature drop to ~10-15.6°C to initiate pinning (out-grow standard, fungiacademy), but out-grow's "warm-weather" strain explicitly needs NO cold shock, and the Thai commercial farm simply moved bottles from 20°C to a 16°C cropping room (a moderate drop, not a hobbyist-style "cold shock").
3. Fruiting temperature: everything from 15°C to 27°C appears somewhere, but the center of gravity across most guides and the two real Thai studies is 16-24°C, with commercial/Asian-hot-climate sources (novamushrooms, naturelion) favoring the cooler 15-20°C end and the one true lowland-tropical commercial paper using 16°C. The Scientia Horticulturae (Atila et al. 2021) abstract explicitly says that above 20°C becomes "a limiting factor" in warm regions/summer — in tension with the out-grow warm-weather strain's claim of fruiting fine at 21-27°C. This is a real breeding/strain difference, not just sloppy sourcing.
4. CO2: pinning trigger ~500-700 ppm and general fruiting ceiling ~500-1000/1100 ppm is highly consistent across 6+ independent grower guides — this is the most reliable number in the dataset. Above that ceiling, guides consistently describe elongated/antler-like/"coral" deformed growth instead of compact pom-poms, matching the brief's premise.
5. Biological efficiency / yield: enormous spread, from 15-25% (mushroomalmanac, conservative hobbyist) up to 78-80% on optimized supplemented substrate (out-grow standard) and a peer-reviewed range cited as "15-80%" depending on substrate. The two Thailand-specific commercial/academic numbers I verified directly are 42.61% BE / 113 g fresh weight per bottle (best treatment, 100% rubber sawdust, PMC10432537) and 85.79-123.7 g/bag (Chiang Mai J. Sci. 2024, also rubber-sawdust based) — these are probably the most relevant "real hot-climate commercial" yield figures for a Malaysia-style operation, since both studies used rubber-tree sawdust, which is the common hardwood byproduct in Malaysia/Thailand/Indonesia/Vietnam.
6. Flushes/rest: 2-3 flushes is the modal answer, but one source says up to 4 and one says 3-4; rest between flushes ranges 1-2 weeks to 2-4 weeks across sources.
7. Max/min tolerable temperature: least well-sourced topic. The most rigorous number is from a Korean peer-reviewed strain study (PMC3755240): optimal mycelial growth at 25°C, with near-zero/no growth at both 15°C and 35°C — i.e., 35°C is a real, independently-verified mycelial ceiling. Hobbyist claims of "kills mycelium above 35°C" and a 25°C-ambient/27°C-core self-heating rule of thumb could not be independently verified (search synthesis only) and should be re-checked before relying on them for a controller's safety cutoff.

Source quality: I found exactly two real "hot-climate commercial farm" primary sources — both Thailand, both lowland (not Cameron Highlands/Genting-style highland): Fresh & Friendly Farm, Pathum Thani province (near Bangkok, PMC10432537/Nature Sci Reports 2023) and the Chiang Mai Journal of Science 2024 trial (also rubber-sawdust based, likely also lowland Thailand). I could not find a published, numeric cultivation protocol specifically from a Malaysian, Indonesian, Vietnamese, Philippine, Taiwanese, southern-Chinese, or Indian lion's-mane farm — only a 2009 Food Technology & Biotechnology paper (Wong et al., ftb.com.hr) confirming H. erinaceus IS cultivated in Malaysia on rubberwood-sawdust+rice-bran bags/logs and is "a temperate mushroom... currently cultivated in Malaysia" (per WebSearch synthesis of that paper's abstract; the PDF itself returned only encoded binary data I could not read, so I could not pull its specific temperature numbers). A China-climatic-zones review (PMC13117637) was blocked by a reCAPTCHA wall and yielded nothing. India and the Philippines/Vietnam/Indonesia only turned up generic highland-vs-lowland strategy advice (elevation 800-2000m / 1500-2200m), not farm-specific numeric protocols — so for those five countries I have essentially no hot-climate-specific primary numbers, only secondary grower-guide generalizations.

Malaysia growers identified (no public per-kg cultivation protocol found for any of them): Mogoo Farm (Klang, Selangor — extraction-powder focused); Mr Fungus (Kuala Lumpur, Pandan Indah — European oak substrate + "Japanese indoor-farming technology," no price listed); 7-Stars Mushroom Farm (Semenyih, Selangor — cold rooms specifically for lion's mane and oyster, per a 2025 mycology-society visit writeup); Shroomy (Kuala Lumpur, grow-kit retailer, per search snippet only); Vegan District and Dusun.com.my are resellers of "local" fresh lion's mane without naming the grower.

Malaysia price data (fresh, retail): RM90/kg (Dusun.com.my, directly fetched, though the page itself has an internal weight inconsistency — titled "(1kg)" but showing 0.2kg/400g/800g pack sizes) and RM100/kg (RM10/100g, Vegan District, directly fetched) are the two numbers I could independently verify by reading the actual page. Mogoo Farm's RM35/300g (≈RM116.67/kg) and the frozen RM25-55 per 400-800g range came only from search-engine snippets, not a page I read directly — flagged accordingly. I found no credible, dated Malaysian farm-gate (wholesale) price, and no credible Malaysian dried-lion's-mane retail price in RM/kg — the closest dried/concentrated figure is an unverified Tridge export-trade snippet of USD 254.94/kg for powdered lion's mane exported from Malaysia (dated 2025-10-21), which is a different, far more concentrated product than dried whole mushroom and should not be treated as a dried-mushroom retail benchmark. No Cameron Highlands- or Genting-specific lion's mane grower or price was found; the "mushroom farms" that do exist in those highland towns (per Tripadvisor/travel-blog results) read as tourist attractions growing other species (shiitake, reishi), not confirmed lion's mane operations.

I was unable to load this run's WebFetch/WebSearch schemas for the China PMC13117637 recaptcha-blocked page, the ftb.com.hr Malaysia PDF (binary/encoded, unreadable by the fetch tool), and the Scientia Horticulturae full text (paywalled, abstract-only via search synthesis) — all three would likely have been the strongest hot-climate-specific sources if accessible.

sweeps.notes:
Read 18 pages directly (WebFetch, or curl+pdftotext for the North Spore PDF) across 16 distinct commercial-grower/spawn-supplier domains: FreshCap (2 pages), North Spore (FAQ page + linked "FruitingBlockBookletUpdated.pdf" instruction booklet, parsed locally with pdftotext since WebFetch can't read binary PDFs), Field Forest Products (4 pages: millet spawn, ready-to-fruit instructions, DIY block instructions, block-set product page), Groovy Pigeon Mycology, Out-Grow (standard strain + "warm weather" specialty-strain pages), Toshifarm, Gourmet Cultures, Bootstrapbee, Grocycle (UK urban mushroom farm), Naturelion.ca, and Liquidfungi. Two more (mushroomgrowinghub.online, mushroomgrowinghub "what temp kills mycelium") were included but flagged lower-confidence since they read as generic SEO blogs rather than a commercial grower/spawn supplier, and their lion's-mane-specific claims are really generic "standard cultivated species" claims, not measured on H. erinaceus itself. Fungi Perfecti (fungi.com) could NOT be verified: both the "Hericium erinaceus Culture" and "Lion's Mane Grain Master Bag" URLs returned genuine HTTP 404s even with a browser user-agent via curl (confirmed by HTML title "404 Not Found" / "Page not found") - the "fruiting temperature 60-80°F" figure attributed to Fungi Perfecti in search-engine summaries should be treated as unverified/possibly stale, since I could not read the actual page. North Spore's grain-spawn product page and Field Forest's millet-spawn product page likewise had no live numeric growing parameters visible in fetched content (likely behind JS-rendered tabs/accordions) beyond the one inoculation-rate figure Field Forest did expose.

KEY DISAGREEMENTS FOUND:
1. Fruiting CO2 ceiling varies by ~300ppm across sources: Groovy Pigeon Mycology says keep CO2 below 800ppm; North Spore's own booklet, Toshifarm, Bootstrapbee and Grocycle all say up to 1,000ppm is fine; Out-Grow's warm-weather page puts the trigger threshold at 1,000-1,100ppm. No source's CO2 number was found to be strain/phase-matched perfectly with another, so treat ~800-1000ppm as the practical "below this" ceiling during fruiting, with primordia initiation wanting the lower end (North Spore: 500-700ppm for primordia specifically, the only source that split CO2 by phase).
2. Fruiting temperature ranges from a cool-strain floor of 55°F/13°C (Field Forest, Liquidfungi) up to a warm-strain ceiling of 80°F/27°C (Out-Grow's purpose-bred "warm weather" Hericium strain). Standard-strain commercial consensus clusters around 60-75°F (15-24°C); FreshCap's pinning-trigger of 15°C and fruiting band of 15-20°C sit at the cooler end, Toshifarm's 16-21°C is similar, while Naturelion.ca calls 16-20°C/60-68°F "the sweet spot."
3. Field Forest Products' own site is internally inconsistent: its "ready-to-fruit blocks" page states fruiting temp 55-65°F/humidity 70-80%, its "make your own blocks" page states fruiting temp 55-70°F/humidity 70-85% and days-to-harvest 10-21 (vs 12-18 on the sister page), and its block-set PRODUCT PAGE contradicts itself in a single page, giving BOTH "55-65°F" and "Ideal Fruiting Temperature...62°-70°F" for temperature, and BOTH ">85%" and "85-90%" for humidity. Treat Field Forest's numbers as a range-of-ranges rather than one fixed spec.
4. Light intensity during fruiting: Toshifarm says keep below 500 lux; Grocycle says 500-1000 lux - direct contradiction on whether 500+ lux is desirable or to be avoided. Hours-of-light recommendations are more consistent (8-12 hrs/day per Field Forest, 12 hrs/day per North Spore, both general not Lion's-Mane-specific for North Spore).
5. Biological efficiency: FreshCap's "90-140% BE" (described by FreshCap itself as showing "strong first-flush potential") is far above the "15-80%" BE range Out-Grow's warm-weather page attributes to peer-reviewed literature depending on substrate. FreshCap's figure reads as an optimistic/marketing best-case rather than a typical grower average; treat the wide 15-140% spread as reflecting substrate quality, supplementation, and strain differences more than a single "true" BE for the species.
6. Cold shock / pinning trigger: no Lion's-Mane-specific source among those read said a literal refrigeration "cold shock" is required. North Spore's own booklet explicitly prescribes refrigeration cold-shock for its Black King and Reishi species pages but not for Lion's Mane, whose own page only says to cut holes in the bag once colonized (fresh air + opening the bag is the trigger). FreshCap's "lower temperature to 15°C" is a modest ambient drop, not refrigeration. This suggests the commercial consensus is: temperature drop + fresh air/CO2 drop triggers pinning, with cold-shock being an optional accelerant some home growers use but not a documented requirement from any supplier read here.
7. No source read gave a quantified CO2 ppm *tolerance specifically during the spawn-run/incubation phase* (as opposed to primordia/fruiting) - colonizing mycelium is universally described only qualitatively as tolerating/needing high CO2 while dark-incubating; the only incubation-phase numeric environmental spec found (besides temperature) was Toshifarm's humidity figure (90-95% RH during incubation) and its core/substrate-temperature figure (ambient 25°C vs substrate/core 27°C) - this is the only direct "block core temperature" data point found among commercial-grower sources; general academic/forum discussion (not independently verified here) suggests metabolic heating of several °C above ambient is typical in bulk blocks, consistent with Toshifarm's 2°C ambient-to-core gap.
8. Source-quality notes: North Spore's PDF booklet is the richest, most species-specific, phase-split (primordia vs fruitbody) data from an actual commercial fruiting-block/spawn supplier, and is the best single primary source found. FreshCap and Naturelion.ca are grow-kit/spawn sellers with clear commercial guides. Toshifarm, Groovy Pigeon Mycology, Bootstrapbee and Grocycle read as grower-blog content (Grocycle is a real commercial urban mushroom farm in the UK). Liquidfungi's own °F-to-°C conversion is internally wrong (states 70°F = 18°C; actual conversion is ~21°C), which is a quality red flag for that source's other numbers. mushroomgrowinghub.online's temperature-kill-threshold numbers are generic across "standard cultivated species" rather than measured for H. erinaceus, so they were included only as general context, clearly flagged, not as species-specific data.

sweeps.notes:
Methodology: used WebSearch to locate candidates, then WebFetch (and pdftotext on PDFs saved by WebFetch, since several PDFs returned garbled text on first pass) to read and quote the actual pages. ~24 distinct source domains were read, well above the 6-source minimum. Several sites (eng-tips.com, renewableenergyhub.co.uk, woodgroup.com, epsmg.jkr.gov.my, kupdf.net) returned HTTP 403/DNS errors on direct WebFetch; for those I report the content via the WebSearch tool's extracted snippet and flag sourceType as "search snippet" rather than a directly-fetched page, so the provenance is honest. No number below was invented — every finding traces to a quote either read directly or surfaced verbatim by the search tool.

Key disagreements / quality notes per topic:
1. Bare zinc/metal roof U-value: no single authoritative figure for "bare sheet" exists in codes (bare sheets are never installed without purlins/insulation in practice). EngineeringToolbox's generic "corrugated metal, uninsulated" figure of 8.5 W/m2K is the most citable number. The Malaysian GBI guidebook's own worked U-value tables confirm the bare metal deck's own thermal resistance is ~0.000 m2K/W (i.e. the sheet itself is thermally negligible; U-value is governed almost entirely by the air films and whatever insulation is added behind it).
2. Brick walls: results are scattered and sometimes counter-intuitive. diydata.com's reference table gives IDENTICAL 2.2 W/m2K for both a 115mm-plastered single-skin wall and a 230mm/9" solid wall — plausible physically (brick's own conductivity is high, so most of the resistance comes from air films and plaster, which barely differ between the two), but it means these two figures should not be treated as firmly distinct. An Indian academic paper (ijcrt.org, citing NBC 2016) gives a much higher 3.15 W/m2K for a 230mm brick wall. UK government/BRE research (gov.scot) on genuine two-brick (215-230mm) solid walls converged on 1.7-2.1 W/m2K (with in-situ measurement supporting ~1.75 W/m2K) — this is a different, generally lower, range than the Indian paper. Expect real Malaysian clay-brick walls to fall somewhere in the wide 1.7-3.15 W/m2K band depending on brick density/moisture and whether plaster/render is included; treat 2.0-2.2 W/m2K as a reasonable mid-estimate for either thickness and don't expect a strong halving of U-value between 115mm and 230mm brick.
3. PU/PIR sandwich panels: the only number I could verify against an actual manufacturer datasheet (Kingspan KS1000RW, PDF) is for PIR foam core, which is chemically a cousin of PU (more fire-resistant, closed-cell) and is what's commercially sold as "PU panel" for cold rooms. That table gives 0.38 W/m2K at 50mm, 0.30/0.25 W/m2K bracketing 75mm (70mm/80mm, no 75mm SKU offered), and 0.20 W/m2K at 100mm. Generic cold-room-panel marketplace listings (made-in-china, etc.) almost never publish a verifiable U-value table — they quote only foam thermal conductivity (lambda ~0.019-0.03 W/mK) or an unlabelled single "heat transfer coefficient" (0.45 W/m2K) without stating the thickness it applies to; treat those as low-confidence marketing numbers.
4. EPS sandwich panels: two manufacturer datasheets disagree by nearly 2x at the same thicknesses - aluminiumextrusions.com.au (Australian, NCC-tested at 23°C): 0.86/0.57/0.42 W/m2K at 50/75/100mm; sunnyda-house.com: 0.57/0.38/0.19 W/m2K at 50/75/100mm. Likely due to different EPS densities/grades or test standards; there is no single "EPS panel" U-value, only a manufacturer-specific one.
5. Malaysia outdoor design conditions: MS 1525:2007 (and unchanged in the 2014 second revision per secondary sources) specifies 33.3°C dry bulb / 27.2°C wet bulb for ACMV peak-load design - this is the standard, authoritative figure to use. The current MS 1525:2019 edition's own front matter explicitly states it revised "the ACMV outdoor design wet bulb temperature" in Annex C, but I could only access the cover/TOC/foreword preview of the 2019 PDF (the full standard sits behind SIRIM paywall), so the new wet-bulb figure is unconfirmed - flagged as an open gap, not invented. Two unrelated secondary figures should not be confused with the ACMV design condition: a Kuala Lumpur annual-maximum climate study cites 34.90°C DB / 26.50°C WB (a different statistic - annual max, not a design percentile), and an outdoor-thermal-comfort study proposes a human-comfort zone of 27.5-33.7°C DB / 50.7-85% RH (a comfort-zone definition, not a cooling-load design condition).
6. ERV/heat-recovery/pre-cooling effectiveness: numbers cluster into three tiers across every source checked - plain aluminum plate exchangers (sensible-only) ~30-75%, run-around coils ~45-65%, and desiccant/enthalpy/thermal wheels (sensible+latent) ~70-85%, with Greenheck's own FAQ (directly fetched, highest-confidence source here) giving the most conservative numbers (30% / 50-60% / 70-80%). One engineer forum thread (eng-tips.com, via snippet) argues a standalone pre-cooling coil (without heat recovery) gives little to no efficiency benefit - a qualitative dissenting view worth weighing against the device-effectiveness percentages.
7. Mushroom foggers/humidifiers: output claims range from 3 L/h (small purpose-built unit for 20-50 m2) to 24 L/h (industrial unit for 350-400 m2), with sizing guides suggesting roughly 200-600+ ml/h per "room size tier" rather than a strict linear L/h-per-m3 rule - none of the sizing guides found scale cleanly to a 60 m3 room, so these are directional, not precise. One product listing (fasalbazar.com) is internally inconsistent (title says "8 LPH," body text says "5 litre per hour" for the same SKU) - flagged, don't rely on it alone.
8. Exhaust/inline fans: for a 60 m3 room, freshfungifarm.com's own two rules of thumb disagree with each other if applied literally: "1 CFM per sq ft of floor" on a 20 m2 (~215 sq ft) floor gives ~215 CFM (~365 m3/h), while its "10-12 ACH" rule on 60 m3 gives 600-720 m3/h - roughly 2x higher. The per-substrate-ton figures (180-300 m3/h per ton, veshenka-expert.info) are a third, independent method based on spawn/block mass rather than room volume, and will likely dominate sizing in a dense small farm. A single commercial 4"-6" inline duct fan (208-688 CFM / 350-1170 m3/h, VIVOSUN AeroZesh S4/S6, directly fetched from manufacturer/retailer pages) comfortably covers any of these targets for a 60 m3 room.

Overall source quality: the most trustworthy figures are the ones read from an actual standard/government document (Malaysian GBI guidebook, MS1525 reproductions, UK gov.scot BRE report), an academic paper (ijcrt.org), a manufacturer's real engineering datasheet (Kingspan PDF, Greenheck FAQ, VIVOSUN manufacturer page), or an engineering reference table (EngineeringToolbox, diydata.com). The weakest-confidence figures are self-reported B2B marketplace listings (made-in-china, alibaba-style pages) and e-commerce product pages for foggers/fans, which are unverified, sometimes internally inconsistent, and should be treated as rough sizing guidance rather than engineering-grade specifications.

sweeps.notes:
Methodology: Loaded WebSearch/WebFetch via ToolSearch, then cross-checked AI-synthesized WebSearch summaries against directly-fetched pages and, for several PDFs, against the Read tool's direct image extraction of the actual paper (not just a model's text summary of it) — this caught a real error (see below) and is why some numbers below are flagged lower-confidence rather than included as findings.

TOP SOURCES (ranked by reliability for this topic):
1. Stamets, P. "Growing Gourmet and Medicinal Mushrooms" (Ten Speed Press, 2000/2011) — the original classic cultivation table (spawn run / primordia formation / fruitbody development / cropping cycle), reproduced verbatim on https://www.shroomery.org/9400/Hericium-erinaceus and independently corroborated by a 2022 peer-reviewed paper (Gonkhom et al., Mycological Progress 21:82, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11557-022-01829-6) which cites the same book and gives matching numbers. This is the most load-bearing source for the full-stage breakdown (T/RH/CO2/FAE/light/days per stage).
2. Chutimanukul et al. 2023, Scientific Reports 13:13316 (Nature) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10432537/ — real commercial-scale tropical bottle-cultivation trial with full yield/BE table across rubber:bamboo sawdust ratios (BE 14.5%–42.6%).
3. Khurana et al. 2022, Annals of Agri-Bio Research 27(2):149-152 — https://agribiop.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/11/149-152.pdf — peer-reviewed (Scopus-indexed, modest-tier regional Indian journal), gives explicit spawn/fruiting T&RH, mycelial-growth-vs-temperature curve (16–32°C), harvest trigger, flush count, and sawdust-vs-straw yield.
4. Gonkhom et al. 2021, Fungal Biotec 1(2):118-130 (review) — https://fungalbiotec.org/pdf/FGBT_1_2_8.pdf — gives days-to-primordia, flush count, and pre-harvest humidity-drop practice, each citing a primary source (Ko et al. 2005; Bunroj et al. 2017; Stamets 2011).
5. Cornell Small Farms Program (university extension) — general (not Hericium-specific) but gives the only quantified spawn-run core-vs-ambient temperature data found (core can run 10-15°F warmer than ambient; ~95°F core "cooks" the mycelium and invites contamination).
6. Figlas, González Matute & Curvetto 2007, Int J Medicinal Mushrooms 9(1):67-73 — the one Hericium-specific sunflower-seed-hull BE trial; I could not get past a 403 on the primary PDF (ResearchGate/Academia.edu/Begell House all blocked WebFetch), but its key BE figure (37.4%, unsupplemented) is independently confirmed via the same authors' 2016 open-access self-citing review (jscimedcentral.com), which I did read directly.

NO MARDI OR FAO SOURCE FOUND: despite multiple targeted searches, no MARDI (Malaysia) or FAO publication specifically on Hericium erinaceus cultivation parameters could be located. Malaysia-specific Hericium work found was from Universiti Malaya and private farms (Ganofarm, Mr Fungus), not MARDI. No Penn State Extension page specifically on Hericium erinaceus was found either (Penn State Extension covers mushroom production generally, not a lion's-mane-specific protocol with numbers).

A CAUGHT ERROR WORTH FLAGGING: one WebSearch summary attributed these numbers to Hericium erinaceus: "colonization 24±1°C/70-80%RH for 10-13 days; fruiting 24±3°C/90-95%RH/12h photoperiod/1500-2000 lux." I fetched the underlying PDF directly and confirmed this data is actually from González-Matute, Figlas, Devalis, Delmastro & Curvetto (2002), "Sunflower seed hulls as a main nutrient source for cultivating Ganoderma lucidum," Micología Aplicada International 14(2):19-24 — i.e. it describes Ganoderma, not Hericium (same Argentine research group, similar methodology, conflated by the search synthesis). I excluded these numbers entirely rather than report them as Hericium data. This is the reason I treat AI-generated WebSearch summaries as lower-confidence than directly-fetched/directly-read page text throughout, and why several numbers below are explicitly flagged as "secondary/unverified."

DISAGREEMENTS:
- Flush count: 2 (Khurana 2022, peer-reviewed; also reported for Figlas 2007 via secondary synthesis: first flush day 10, second day 30, 55-day total cycle) vs 3–4 per bag (Bunroj et al. 2017, cited in Gonkhom 2021 review) vs 2–3 ("first flush largest," Out-Grow commercial cultivar sheet) vs "up to 4 flushes documented" (Out-Grow standard species page, not independently verified against a primary study).
- Light during spawn run: the classic Stamets table lists "n/a" for spawn-run light (implying darkness is standard/optional), and several grower guides explicitly say darkness prevents premature fruiting — yet Chutimanukul et al. 2023 (peer-reviewed, Scientific Reports) explicitly incubated "in the presence of light" at 20°C during colonization. This is a genuine contradiction between a peer-reviewed commercial trial and the conventional/classic guidance.
- CO2 ceiling for fruiting: most sources (Stamets table, multiple grower guides) converge on roughly 500-1,000 ppm; the Out-Grow "warm weather" cultivar sheet states <1,100 ppm; assorted uncited grower blogs claim morphological failure thresholds anywhere from 800 to 1,500+ ppm (coral/elongated spines below that, primordia abortion above ~1,500 ppm per one blog). I could not find any controlled, peer-reviewed dose-response study that measures spine length/branching as a function of CO2 ppm for H. erinaceus specifically — this appears to be an evidence gap in the literature, with practical guidance resting on grower experience rather than published experiments.
- Biological efficiency is highly substrate/strain dependent and spans roughly 14.5% (100% bamboo sawdust, Chutimanukul 2023) to 37.4-43.1% (sunflower seed hulls, Figlas 2007/2016 — the 43.1% Mn/NH4-supplemented figure and the day-10/day-30/55-day flush timeline came only from WebSearch synthesis of the 2007 paper, not a page I could independently fetch, so treat with more caution than the 37.4% figure) to 42.6% (100% rubber sawdust, Chutimanukul 2023) to a reported 45.5% (sawdust 70%+wheat bran 30%, Jahedi et al. 2023/2024, Scientia Horticulturae 323:112510 — also only accessed via secondary synthesis, primary ScienceDirect page 403'd) up to a claimed 88.4% BE on eucalyptus sawdust (276.19 and 245.10 g/bag) — this last figure traces back through at least two layers of citation (found quoted inside a WebSearch summary of the Jahedi paper, which itself was citing an earlier, unidentified primary study) and its ultimate primary source could not be confirmed; I did not include it as a findings-array entry because of this weak chain of custody, but flag it here since the task asked to record disagreements.
- Temperature-tolerance ceiling: no single peer-reviewed number for "the" maximum fruiting temperature before yellowing/browning was found. Best available quantified proxies: Khurana et al. 2022 show mycelial dry-weight growth collapsing from 5.95 g (24°C) to 0.68 g (32°C) — a clear thermal ceiling for vegetative growth; practical/commercial sources (Out-Grow) sell a heat-tolerant "warm weather" cultivar fruiting at 21-27°C specifically because standard strains reportedly fail to pin/fruit reliably above roughly 22-25°C, but no peer-reviewed study quantifying the exact yellowing/browning threshold in degrees was located.
- Days from pinning to harvest: terms are used inconsistently across sources. Stamets' "Fruitbody Development: 4-5 days" measures only the final primordia-to-maturity growth phase of one flush. Separately, Ko et al. 2005 (cited in Gonkhom 2021) report 33-40 days from spawning to primordia appearance, plus 10 more days to first harvest (~43-50 days total), and Chutimanukul et al. 2023 independently report 47 days total from spawning to harvest — broadly consistent with Ko et al. but much longer than the "4-5 days" figure, which is not directly comparable since it excludes the spawn-run and early-primordia period.

SOURCE-ACCESS CAVEATS: Figlas et al. 2007 (Int J Medicinal Mushrooms), Atila et al. 2021 (Scientia Horticulturae 280:109915 — tested Hericium fruiting at 15°C/20°C/25°C, found protein content and yield varied by isolate and temperature, e.g. "He-Ankara" protein peaked at 19.7% at 20°C), and Jahedi et al. 2023/2024 (Scientia Horticulturae 323:112510) were all paywalled/403-blocked on every mirror I tried (ResearchGate, Academia.edu, ScienceDirect, Begell House); their numbers above came from consistent multi-query WebSearch synthesis rather than a page I personally read, except where corroborated by a directly-read companion document (Figlas 2016 review). Treat the 43.1% BE, day-10/day-30/55-day cycle, 45.5% BE, and eucalyptus 88.4% BE figures accordingly.
